name: oom-chain
notes: Host memory climbs from 70% through the 90% pressure boundary to the 98% limit boundary; the two crossings are one episode (ESCALATES_TO), not a causal claim.
The worker exit at T+30s is recorded, but v1 bundles carry no kernel OOM record, so no edge may connect the limit to that exit.
No OOM_EVENT is fabricated; the unexplained exit and the unrecovered limit are two UNKNOWN anchors, and only the exit carries the 'OOM suspected' alternative.

Re-audit 2026-10-28 (principal, causal-semantics.md §5.2 clarified): a failure is never its own candidate, and an escalation-only path is the anchor's own episode (known chain), not a contributing factor. Suspected-kill/write-failure alternatives explain exit failures only, never a condition anchor.

missing_evidence_includes: the originating allocation growth (or a kernel OOM record) is not captured in v1 bundles
exit status and signal lineage are not captured in v1 bundles
alternatives: OOM suspected; kernel OOM record not captured
